(men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]] | highlights = * [[All-NBA G League Team|All-NBA G League First Team]] ([[2024–25 NBA G League season|2025]]) * [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional Scoring Champion|BSN scoring champion]] (2026) *[[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-12 Player of the Year]] ([[2018–19 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|2019]]) *First-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] (2019) }} '''Jaylen Clinton Andrew Nowell''' (born July 9, 1999{{cite web|title=Jaylen Nowell|work=Twitter.com|url=https://twitter.com/jaylennowell?lang=en|access-date=March 12, 2019}}) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) and the [[EuroLeague]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington Huskies]] of the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12 Conference]], and was named the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|conference's player of the year]] in 2019. He was selected by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in the second round of the [[2019 NBA draft]]. ==Early life== Nowell was born in [[Seattle]] to Lanie and Mike Nowell.{{cite web|first=Dan|last=Bell|title=Minnesota Timberwolves 2019–20 Media Guide|url=https://www.nba.com/resources/static/team/v2/timberwolves/2019-20WolvesMediaGuide_LR.pdf|website=NBA.com|publisher=Minnesota Timberwolves|year=2019|page=30|access-date=March 12, 2019|quote=BIRTHDATE: April 4, 1999 in Seattle, Washington}}{{cite news|first=Brian|last=Hamilton|title='His game screams': Why Washington's Jaylen Nowell can't stop|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/849840/2019/03/06/his-game-screams-why-washingtons-jaylen-nowell-cant-stop/|url-access=subscription|work=The Athletic|date=March 6, 2019|access-date=March 12, 2019|quote=Mike Nowell stood 6-6 and weighed anywhere from 250 to 260 pounds when he played, walking proof of F = m x a and a bulwark post player who set such emphatic screens that he’d knock the wind out of defenders who ran into him.}} His parents met at [[Clark Atlanta University]], where they both played basketball. His father played professionally in the [[Continental Basketball Association]]. Jaylen Nowell attended high school in Seattle at [[Garfield High School (Seattle)|Garfield High]], where he was a standout player.{{cite news|first=Theo|last=Lawson|title=Washington State assistant, ex-Garfield coach Ed Haskins preparing for reunion with Washington's Jaylen Nowell|url=http://www.spokesman.com/stories/2018/jan/05/washington-state-assistant-ex-garfield-coach-ed-ha/|newspaper=The Spokesman-Review|date=January 5, 2018|access-date=March 12, 2019}} ==College career== At the [[University of Washington]], Nowell was originally part of a five-player [[college recruiting|recruiting]] class considered the best in the [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Huskies]]' history. However, after Washington coach [[Lorenzo Romar]] was fired, he was the lone member who remained committed to the school and first-year coach [[Mike Hopkins (basketball)|Mike Hopkins]].{{cite news|first=Christian|last=Caple|title=Garfield's Nowell sticks with UW|url=https://www.kitsapsun.com/story/sports/college/2017/04/18/garfields-nowell-sticks-uw/100628974/|newspaper=The News Tribune|date=April 18, 2017|access-date=March 12, 2019}} As a freshman in [[2017–18 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|2017–18]], Nowell averaged 16.0 points per game.{{cite news|first=Matt|last=Calkins|title=Huskies star Jaylen Nowell has gotten even better — and smarter|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/uw-husky-basketball/calkins-column-on-uw-basketball-player-jaylen-nowell/|newspaper=The Seattle Times|date=January 17, 2019|access-date=March 12, 2019}} The [[2018–19 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|following season]], he was named the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-12 Player of the Year]] after leading the Huskies in scoring and helping them win the Pac-12 regular season championship.{{cite news|first=Percy|last=Allen|title=Huskies win top three Pac-12 postseason awards: Jaylen Nowell is player of the year|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/uw-husky-basketball/uws-matisse-thybulle-and-jaylen-nowell-voted-first-team-all-pac-12/|newspaper=The Seattle Times|date=March 11, 2019|access-date=March 12, 2019}} Following Washington's loss in the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2019 NCAA men's basketball tournament]], Nowell announced his intention to forgo his final two seasons of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2019 NBA draft]]. ==Professional career== ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2019–2023)=== On June 20, 2019, Nowell was selected with the 43rd overall pick in the 2nd round by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in the [[2019 NBA draft]].{{cite web|title=TIMBERWOLVES SELECT TWO PLAYERS IN 2019 NBA DRAFT|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-select-two-players-2019-nba-draft|website=NBA.com|date=June 20, 2019|access-date=June 20, 2019}} He was later included in the Timberwolves' roster for the [[2019 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|title=TIMBERWOLVES ANNOUNCE MGM RESORTS NBA SUMMER LEAGUE 2019 IN LAS VEGAS ROSTER|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-announce-mgm-resorts-nba-summer-league-2019-las-vegas-roster|website=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2019|access-date=July 1, 2019}} On August 6, Nowell signed with the Timberwolves.{{cite web|title=TIMBERWOLVES SIGN JAYLEN NOWELL|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-jaylen-nowell|website=NBA.com|date=August 6, 2019|access-date=August 6, 2019}} He made his NBA debut on November 6, playing one minute in a 121–137 loss to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|first=Cay|last=Bailey|title=BROOKS, MORANT HELP GRIZZLIES BEAT TIMBERWOLVES 137-121|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900108|website=NBA.com|date=November 7, 2019|access-date=February 5, 2023}} On January 1, 2020, Nowell scored a season-high 12 points, alongside two rebounds, in a 104–106 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|first=Andrew|last=Wagner|title=ANTETOKOUNMPO SCORES 32, BUCKS HOLD OFF WOLVES 106-104|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900506|website=NBA.com|date=January 2, 2020|access-date=February 5, 2023}} On March 11, 2021, Nowell scored a season-high 28 points, alongside five rebounds and six assists, in a 135–105 win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web|first=Brett|last=Martel|title=NOWELL HAS CAREER NIGHT, TIMBERWOLVES ROUT PELICANS 135-105|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000574|website=NBA.com|date=March 11, 2021|access-date=February 5, 2023}} On December 27, 2021, Nowell scored a career-high 29 points, alongside six rebounds and three assists, in a 108–103 win over the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|first=Patrick|last=Donnelly|title=SHORT-HANDED T-WOLVES SNAP 2-GAME SKID, BEAT CELTICS 108-103|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100503|website=NBA.com|date=December 27, 2021|access-date=February 5, 2023}} The Timberwolves qualified for the postseason for the first time since [[2018 NBA playoffs|2018]] and faced the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] during their first round series. Nowell made his playoff debut on April 19, 2022, scoring six points in a 96–124 Game 2 loss.{{cite web|first=Teresa M.|last=Walker|title=GRIZZLIES ROUT TIMBERWOLVES 124-96 TO TIE SERIES AT 1 APIECE|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042100152|website=NBA.com|date=April 20, 2022|access-date=February 5, 2023}} The Timberwolves were eliminated by the Grizzlies in six games. ===Stockton Kings / Memphis Grizzlies (2023–2024)=== On October 2, 2023, Nowell signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]],{{cite web|title=Kings Announce 2023-24 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-announce-2023-24-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 2, 2023|access-date=October 2, 2023}} but was waived on October 20.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Kings Waiving Jaylen Nowell, Two Others|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/10/kings-waiving-jaylen-nowell-two-others.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 20, 2023|access-date=October 22, 2023}}{{cite web|title=NBA Player Transactions {{!}} NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/players/transactions|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 21, 2023}} On November 9, he was named to the opening night roster for the [[Stockton Kings]].{{cite web|title=Stockton Kings Announce 2023-24 Opening Night Roster|url=https://stockton.gleague.nba.com/news/stockton-kings-announce-2023-24-opening-night-roster|website=NBA.com|date=November 9, 2023|access-date=November 9, 2023}} On November 24, 2023, Nowell signed a 10-day contract with the Grizzlies{{cite web|title=Grizzlies sign Jaylen Nowell and Shaquille Harrison to 10-day contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-sign-jaylen-nowell-and-shaquille-harrison-to-10-day-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=November 24, 2023|access-date=November 24, 2023}} and on December 4, he signed a second 10-day deal.{{cite web|title=Grizzlies sign Jaylen Nowell to second 10-day contract|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-sign-jaylen-nowell-to-second-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=December 4, 2023|access-date=December 5, 2023}} On December 15, he returned to Stockton.{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Stockton Kings Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Stockton-Kings/56/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 16, 2023}} ===Detroit Pistons (2024)=== On April 3, 2024, Nowell signed a 10-day contract with the [[Detroit Pistons]]{{cite tweet|author=Pistons PR|title=The @DetroitPistons announced today that the team has signed guard Jaylen Nowell to a 10-day contract.|number=1775521571412627880|user=Pistons_PR|date=April 3, 2024|access-date=April 3, 2024}} and on April 13, he signed a second 10-day contract.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Pistons Sign Jaylen Nowell To Second Hardship Deal|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/04/pistons-to-sign-jaylen-nowell-to-second-hardship-deal.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=April 13, 2024|access-date=April 13, 2024}} On September 29, 2024, Nowell signed with the [[Washington Wizards]],{{cite web|title=Wizards Announce 2024 Training Camp Roster/Schedule|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-announce-2024-training-camp-roster-schedule|website=NBA.com|date=September 29, 2024|access-date=September 30, 2024}} but was waived on October 10.{{cite tweet|author=Wizards PR|title=Official: The Washington Wizards have waived G Jaylen Nowell.|number=1844408912709407124|user=WizPRStats|date=October 10, 2024|access-date=October 10, 2024}} On October 28, he joined the [[Capital City Go-Go]]{{cite web|title=Go-Go Announce Training Camp Roster, Dates|url=https://capitalcity.gleague.nba.com/news/go-go-announce-training-camp-roster-dates-2|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=November 3, 2024}} === New Orleans Pelicans (2024) === On November 3, 2025, Nowell signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web|title=Pelicans sign Jaylen Nowell|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/jaylen-nowell-guard-new-orleans-pelicans-roster-signing-november-3-2024|website=NBA.com|date=November 3, 2024|access-date=November 3, 2024}} However, he was waived on November 20.{{cite web|title=Pelicans sign Elfrid Payton|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/elfrid-payton-signed-new-orleans-pelicans-roster-november-20-2024|website=NBA.com|date=November 20, 2024|access-date=November 20, 2024}} === Capital City Go-Go (2024–2025) === On November 20, 2024, Nowell signed with the [[Capital City Go-Go]] for a second time.{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Capital City Go-Go Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Capital-City-Go-Go/55/Transaction-History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=November 24, 2024}} On February 8, 2025, Nowell signed a 10-day contract with the [[Washington Wizards]], but did not appear in a game for them.{{Cite web |date=February 8, 2025 |title=Washington Signs Jaylen Nowell to 10-Day Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/washington-signs-jaylen-nowell-to-10-day-contract |access-date=2025-02-09 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} Following the expiration of his 10-day contract, he returned to the Go-Go. === Shanxi Loongs (2025–2026) === On June 9, 2025, Nowell signed with the [[Shanxi Loongs]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA).{{cite web | last=Cassels | first=Eamon | title=Former Timberwolves draft pick lands surprise new job away from the NBA | website=Dunking with Wolves|publisher=FanSided | date=2025-06-10 | url=https://dunkingwithwolves.com/jaylen-nowell-new-job-away-from-nba | access-date=2025-12-07}} ===Beşiktaş (2026–present)=== On July 12, 2026, Nowell signed with [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite tweet |user=BJK_Basketbol |number=2076320063380988100 |title=Resmi Açıklama Jaylen Nowell}} ==Career statistics==
